checks.finding: No issues found. design.md's Design Decisions section justifies every material judgment call with an explicit rationale and source trace: contracts/ over sdd/ placement (INV-010, 'every existing file under contracts/ is JSON (13/13)'), flat top-level gates[] array (INV-003, ADR-0017's own schema example), rejection of a new plugins/sdd-capability/ plugin in favor of the existing plugins/sdd-quality-loop/ (INV-015, avoids duplicating a 3-environment packaging obligation), script-relative Registry discovery over a runtime env var (INV-016/orchestrator ruling P10, 'requires no per-runtime environment variable at all'), Python-master+sh/ps1(+js)-wrapper convention (INV-014, sdd-hook-guard precedent), and JSON-only projection over 4-language generation (Open Questions: 'no consumer for a .py/.js/.sh/.ps1 rendering of the Registry has been identified'). No 'we will use X' statement was found lacking a because/since clause.

Two entries in the Open Questions material fail the required owner/blocks-implementation/resolution-path shape. (1) OQ-004 status is internally contradictory across the two Open-Questions-owning artifacts: investigation.md's own Open Questions section states 'Status: **open, materially expanded** (orchestrator ruling 2026-07-22)' for OQ-004, but the same document's Adversarial Spec Review Response section for the identical OQ-004 states '**fully closed same day per orchestrator ruling P8**', and design.md's Design Decisions section independently asserts '...fully closed 2026-07-22 — orchestrator ruling P8' while design.md's own '## Open Questions' section still lists OQ-004 as 'carried forward from investigation.md ... not re-litigated here, only indexed'. requirements.md directs reviewers to investigation.md's Open Questions section as the status source of truth ('OQ-002/OQ-003 resolved by orchestrator ruling 2026-07-22, see investigation.md's Open Questions section'), so a reviewer following that pointer reads a 'Status: open' line for an item design.md elsewhere calls fully closed — an implementer cannot determine from the documented status field alone whether OQ-004 blocks starting REQ-003(c)'s task. (2) design.md's '## Open Questions' section's fifth, unnumbered entry ('whether the generated projection should mirror guard-invariants' full four-language generation ... or ship only the JSON projection') carries no owner (no role or person named to make or ratify the JSON-only call), no 'Blocks Implementation: yes/no' statement, and no 'Resolution Path:' — it states a design-time leaning ('API / Contract Plan proposes JSON-only') but never records who accepts that as final or what action would close it, meeting this check's 'An open question with no owner is a Major finding' criterion directly.

design.md has a '## Constraint Compliance' section (lines 952-964), so the Primary/TYPE-D rule applies: every constraint listed in requirements.md must be addressed inside that section specifically. The section contains exactly three bullets (Gate-stage scope per ADR-0017 item 1; no plugin/script/contract/test/.github file touched by this spec commit, AC-034; no new plugin introduced). It omits at least three explicit 'must'-level constraints stated elsewhere in requirements.md: (a) REQ-002's forbidden-operator constraint ('Every operator forbidden by ADR-0020 (regex, arbitrary JSONPath, shell, JS, Python, dynamic code, Provider API calls, time-/network-dependent conditions) must be structurally inexpressible in the DSL's own grammar, not merely undocumented', requirements.md:223-226); (b) REQ-003(g)'s Provider-name-contamination boundary (ADR-0018, 'any match fails validation', requirements.md:288-295); (c) the cross-runtime byte-identical-output/determinism constraint (AC-031/AC-032/AC-033, e.g. requirements.md:667-673 'have golden-fixture parity tests proving their .sh- and .ps1-wrapper invocations produce byte-identical output'). All three are real, security/regulatory/compatibility-flavored constraints from requirements.md, and all three are discussed only outside the Constraint Compliance section (in Global Constraints, Security Boundaries, and Test Strategy), never restated or cross-referenced inside it. A reader relying on '## Constraint Compliance' as the canonical compliance checklist (its evident purpose, matching this check's own contract) would conclude only three constraints apply to this design, missing determinism, no-dynamic-evaluation, and provider-neutrality. This is not deferred with a stated rationale anywhere in the section — it is simply absent from it.
